title: Early Balinese Kingdoms
capsule: The earliest securely dated Balinese polity is attested by the Belanjong pillar inscription of 914 CE, erected by King Śrī Kesarī Warmadewa near Sanur. The Warmadewa dynasty reached its widest cultural influence under King Udayana, who married the Javanese princess Mahendradatta of the Isyana dynasty around 990; their son Airlangga later unified much of Java. Balinese independence was interrupted when the Singhasari king Kertanegara launched a military expedition in 1284, and definitively ended in 1343 when Majapahit forces under Gajah Mada defeated King Bedaulu and installed a vassal dynasty at Samprangan by 1344.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the polity is reconstructed primarily from epigraphic sources and Javanese chronicles, and the geographic scope of its control beyond the Balinese heartland is uncertain.
